target: Elle le connaît depuis longtemps.
english: She has known him for a long time.
tip: Depuis wants the present, not the past: elle le connaît depuis longtemps = she has known him a long time. Started back then and still true? French stays in present tense.

target: C'est pour toi, joyeux anniversaire !
tip: After a preposition, te turns into toi: c'est pour toi, never 'pour te'. Once a word like pour or avec comes first, French switches to the stressed pronoun.

target: Il les a appeles ce matin.
tip: The -s on appelés is doing grammar: when a direct object (les) sits before avoir, the participle agrees with it. Les = them (masc.), so appelé gains an s.

target: Je leur en ai parlé hier.
english: I talked to them about it yesterday.
tip: Two pronouns stack in a fixed order before the verb: leur en, never 'en leur'. Here leur = to them and en = about it: je leur en ai parlé.

target: Elle lui parle souvent au téléphone.
english: She often talks to him/her on the phone.
tip: 'lui' means both 'to him' and 'to her' – one word covers either gender, and it parks in front of the verb: 'lui parle', never 'parle à lui'.

target: Elles se sont assises à la terrasse.
tip: S'asseoir: elles se sont assises. Irregular with feminine plural agreement.

target: Tu en as combien chez toi ?
english: How many do you have at home?
tip: Counting forces an 'en': 'Tu en as combien' carries a 'of them' that English drops – 'how many do you have (of them)'.

target: Nous nous promenons dans le parc chaque dimanche.
english: We take a walk in the park every Sunday.
tip: Se promener = to take a walk. Nous nous promenons: first nous is subject, second is reflexive pronoun.

target: La maison a été construite par mon grand-père.
english: The house was built by my grandfather.
tip: In the passive, the participle agrees with the subject: 'construite' takes an -e because 'la maison' is feminine.

target: Elles se sont mises d'accord.
tip: To agree is 'put yourselves in agreement': se mettre d'accord. Elles se sont mises d'accord = they came to an agreement, literally placed themselves in accord.

target: Elle s'est habillée rapidement pour partir au travail.
english: She got dressed quickly to leave for work.
tip: Reflexive verbs build the past with 'être', and the participle agrees with the subject: 'elle s'est habillée' picks up an -e for elle.

target: Ne les ouvre pas.
tip: A negative command keeps the pronoun in front: ne les ouvre pas. Flip to a positive order and it jumps behind with a hyphen: ouvre-les.

target: Il la cherché partout.
tip: Chercher already means 'look for', so the 'for' is built in – it takes a plain object: il la cherche partout, never 'chercher pour'.

target: Donne-le-moi, s'il te plaît.
tip: Positive commands tack pronouns on with hyphens, and me turns into moi: donne-le-moi – the thing (le) first, the person (moi) second.

target: Tu lui ressembles beaucoup.
english: You look a lot like him/her.
tip: French 'resembles TO' someone: 'ressembler à'. So the pronoun is 'lui' (to him/her), not 'le': 'tu lui ressembles'.

target: Je te rappelle ce soir.
tip: No 'will' required – French often uses the plain present for a set plan: je te rappelle ce soir = I'll call you back tonight.

target: Il me comprend très bien.
tip: Object pronouns land BEFORE the verb: il me comprend = he understands me, literally 'he me understands'.

target: Tu en manges souvent ?
tip: English can drop 'some', French can't: 'do you eat often?' still needs en standing in for it – tu en manges souvent ?

target: Elle en a commandé cinq.
tip: Quirk: a preceding en never makes the participle agree. Elle en a commandé cinq stays commandé, no s – unlike les a commandés.

target: Nous les attendons depuis midi.
english: We've been waiting for them since noon.
tip: 'Les' replaces plural direct objects: 'nous les attendons' = we wait for them.

target: Elle en a repris deux fois.
tip: Reprendre at the table means take another helping; en stands for the food: elle en a repris deux fois = she had seconds twice.

target: Elle a terminé par un dessert.
tip: Terminer par = to finish with. Par introduces what comes at the end.

target: J'en ai besoin pour le travail.
tip: Avoir besoin DE hides a de, so 'need it' brings the it back as en: j'en ai besoin = literally 'I have need OF it'.

target: Tu lui téléphones ce soir ?
tip: You phone TO someone in French: téléphoner à quelqu'un. That à becomes lui – tu lui téléphones, not 'tu la téléphones'.

target: Il leur a raconté une histoire.
tip: Leur here is the pronoun 'to them', not the possessive leurs – so it never takes an s: il leur a raconté une histoire, plural yet still leur.

target: Je le lui ai déjà dit.
tip: Double pronouns: le + lui. Le comes before lui or leur.

target: Elle ne me l'a jamais dit.
tip: Two object pronouns stack before the verb, me then le, and le clips to l' before a vowel: elle ne me l'a jamais dit.

target: Elle est sortie par la fenêtre.
english: She went out through the window.
tip: Sortir builds its past with être, not avoir, so the participle agrees with the subject: elle est sortie – that e marks 'she'.

target: Je la vois partir chaque matin.
english: I see her leave every morning.
tip: See someone do something = voir + a bare infinitive: je la vois partir. La is who you see, partir is the action, no 'to'.

target: Tu la regardes depuis cinq minutes.
english: You've been watching her for five minutes.
tip: Depuis takes the present where English needs 'have been': tu la regardes depuis cinq minutes = you've been watching for five minutes.
